evidence.claim: The flagged transaction 3450629 ($100.09, online, product R, region 204.0) sits well inside the card's baseline as of opening: prior median amount $199.97 and prior maximum $2,892.12 over the card's 52 prior transactions (card_seq-1).
The case-memory calibrated score on the flagged transaction is cms_p=0.0987, far below the real-time risk_score of 0.57 that triggered review.
Billing region 204.0 is a region the card already knows: 5 prior purchases over 4 days before opening (region_history hint='known'), not a novel or roaming region.
The purchaser email domain anonymous.com had been used 28 times on this card before the flagged transaction (case_context.txn.prior_pem=28), making it the card's usual domain rather than a new one.

The device profile Windows | Windows 10 | chrome 65.0 | 1920x1080 was already known to this card: 3 prior uses since first seen 2016-10-27, with device_new values Found and New recorded, so the flagged 'Found' use is not a first-time device.

One prior risk-score alert on this card, CC-1383, was cleared under the 'cleared_travel' template, the same shape of alert as this case, with no confirmed prior fraud on the card (n_prior_fraud_cases=0).

recurring_charge_check found 9 prior purchases within ±1% of $100.09 under product code R, 5 of them at anonymous.com over a median 15-day gap (gap CV 1.15, failing the strict R7 monthly-cadence test but showing this price point recurs habitually on the card), inferred from product code, amount, place and cadence since there is no merchant field.

The device profile is widely shared (299 cards all-time, 238 in the 30 days before opening) and touches 7 fraud cases, but shared_origin_scan confirms it is not strong (is_strong=False), so per policy it cannot count as R6 shared-origin evidence despite the elevated fraud-case count.
